governance.note: Carries every caiso-51 keeper lever unchanged (measured WECC per-hub seam decomposition with firm/contracted tranches at documented contract costs, measured p95 corridor envelopes, published MIC seam limit, citygate gas basis, EIA-930 monthly hydro budgets, CAMPD historic outage windows, RA min-load 0.26, UC startup bridge/decommit). This run REMOVES forcing rather than adding levers (legitimacy audit S2): (1) the CAISO CT_PEAKER/CT_CHP netload reliability-floor registry limbs are retired — an A/B against hour-windowed limbs showed them redundant with the net-load drag on the same driver, hours and class (one mechanism per phenomenon, audit rule 18) — leaving ct_netload_drag (h15-21, net-load-proportional, forward-derivable) as the single evening CT commitment mechanism; (2) RA must-offer bridge eligibility is gated on unit physics (min_down_hours >= 4) instead of the hard-coded (CC_REGULAR, CT_PEAKER) class tuple, so fast-start CTs are never economically bridged overnight (audit §1.2c, rule 17). No adder, haircut, or rescale tuned to any residual; the C1/C3 regressions vs caiso-51 are the disclosed cost of removing the flat CT floor (rule #1) — open root-cause item: evening CT merit dispatch (P1 merit order: import tranche prices / CC offers, caiso-48 next-levers thread).
